network.description: Typed per-node `NetworkConfig` diff. Empty map elided.

removals.description:
Removal ops from the plan diff (deleted nodes, links, VRF-table
routes, …), one description per op. Elided when empty.

schema_version.description:
Schema marker: `3`. v3 dropped the v1 `diff` / `layered_summary`
fields (Plan 160 / 0.7.0) — use `topology` / `network` /
`nftables` / `wireguard` / `removals`. `topology` and `wireguard`
were added later and are additive, so the marker did not move.

topology.description:
Lab-graph changes: nodes, links, routes, sysctls, nftables,
impairments, per-pair `impair` matrices, `qdisc` blocks, rate
limits — what the topology files differ in. The kernel side of a
traffic-control change is in `network` (the qdiscs and trees it
declares), with any drift from it (#108). Elided when empty.

wireguard.description:
Typed per-node `WireguardConfigDiff`: peers, keys, endpoints and
allowed-ips that differ from the declared tunnels (public keys
only; private and preshared keys as presence flags). Empty map
elided. Additive, so the marker stays `3`. Free-form in the
schema: nlink 0.32 derives one that does not match the JSON (keys
as byte arrays, presence flags as keys; marcpardo/nlink#876).

params.description: tc(8)'s words for it: `egress redirect dev ifb0`.

AddressRepr.description:
Serde shadow for [`DeclaredAddress`] — the human-facing
`{ dev, address: "<cidr>" }` form. Also the schema source for
[`DeclaredAddress`] (see its manual `JsonSchema` impl).

metric.description: The metric of the prefix route.

peer.description: The other end of a point-to-point address.

preferred-lft.description: The preferred lifetime; the valid one when absent.

valid-lft.description:
The valid lifetime (`"3600s"`, in tc(8)'s time units); forever when
absent.

Blocker.description:
One reason a link cannot be recreated (#513): something deleting it
would destroy that the config does not declare, or a link that cannot
be recreated at all.

oneOf.description:
An address the config does not declare, on the link or on one the
kernel deletes or flushes with it.
A route the config does not declare through the link.

nhid.description: The nexthop object it uses, if any.

protocol.description:
Who added it (`ip route`'s `proto`): a routing daemon re-learns
its own routes, so a [`RecreatePolicy`] may let those go.

through.description:
How it goes through the device, when not as its output
device (`"via a nexthop object on"`, …).

oneOf.description:
A qdisc the config does not declare, or one under a class, which
it cannot declare.

under.description: Its handle and parent, for one under a class.

oneOf.description: A class someone made (HTB, HFSC, DRR, QFQ, CBQ).
An FDB entry a user or a controller made.

via.description:
The link it sends through, when it is on another device: it
would point at the deleted link's old ifindex.

oneOf.description: A permanent or externally learned neighbour.

A link stacked on the recreated one, which the kernel deletes with
it, and which the config does not create.

declared-existing.description:
The config declares it, but as an existing device, not one to
create.

oneOf.description: A port the kernel releases when its master is deleted.

A veth's or vxcan's peer in another namespace, which the kernel
deletes with it and nothing here can declare.

link.description: The link whose peer it is.

netnsid.description: The peer's namespace, as this one numbers it.

oneOf.description:
The link cannot be recreated at all: a device with no link kind,
a pair whose peer a recreate would delete, ….

BridgeOptions.description:
A bridge's options: a link's `bridge` section (#516). Each one unset is
the kernel's and not compared. Build with [`LinkBuilder::bridge_options`].

Bytes.description: A size, as tc(8) writes it ("32kib", "1mb"), or a number of bytes.

ChainName.description:
A validated nftables chain name.

Chain identity in nftables is a `(family, table_name, chain_name)`
triple, all case-sensitive. The kernel enforces
`NFT_NAME_MAXLEN = 256` (per
`include/uapi/linux/netfilter/nf_tables.h`) and rejects interior
NULs (the attribute is a NUL-terminated C string at the wire layer).

Construction validates:
- Non-empty.
- No interior NUL bytes (`\0`).
- At most 255 bytes (one byte reserved for the NUL terminator).

Round-trip note: `ChainName` is `Display` for natural use in
log messages and `AsRef<str>` so it slots into existing
`&str`-shaped APIs.

ChainRecreate.description:
A chain the diff deletes and creates again, with its declared rules put
back in declared order (#478).

`nf_tables_updchain` refuses a different hook, priority or type, and a
hook on a regular chain, with `EEXIST`; and nothing turns a base chain
into a regular one. So these changes were sent as an update the kernel
always refused, and a base chain declared as a regular one stayed a base
chain with an empty diff. A base chain cannot be a jump target, so only
its own rules depend on it.

blocked_by.description:
Rules in the chain that nlink did not write, which it could not put
back. Non-empty means the apply refuses, with
[`ErrorDetail::NotSupported`](crate::ErrorDetail::NotSupported), rather than
delete them. An [`exclusive`](super::DeclaredChainBuilder::exclusive)
chain deletes them instead.

ChainType.description: Chain type string for the kernel.

params.description: tc(8)'s words for its parameters: `rate 60mbit ceil 100mbit`.

parent.description: The qdisc (`1:`) or class (`1:1`) it hangs under.

ConfigDiff.description:
Difference between desired and current network state.

`#[non_exhaustive]` since 0.24 (#165): new `*_to_add` /
`*_to_remove` categories can appear without a major bump.
Construct via [`NetworkConfig::diff`](super::NetworkConfig::diff),
not literally.

addresses-to-change.description:
Addresses whose metric, lifetimes or (IPv6) flags the apply changes
in place (#516). An IPv4 label or flag change cannot be made in
place: the address is then removed and added again.

addresses-to-remove.description:
Addresses to remove (purge mode only — see
[`PlanOptions::purge`]). Populated **only** when the diff is
computed via
[`NetworkConfig::diff_with_options`](crate::netlink::config::NetworkConfig::diff_with_options)
with `purge` on; the default
[`diff`](crate::netlink::config::NetworkConfig::diff) never
removes anything. Kernel-managed addresses (IPv6 link-local,
loopback, any non-`global` scope, anything with a lifetime) are
excluded, and only the interfaces the config declares and
[`PlanOptions::purge_address_devs`] are touched.

fdb-to-remove.description:
FDB entries the previous config declared and this one does not,
still in the kernel (#516). Only with [`PlanOptions::previous`].

fdb-to-set.description:
FDB entries to install (#516): a bridge entry missing, learned or
in the other state (static or local), a VXLAN remote missing — or
on a port the apply moves out of its bridge, or a device it
recreates, which loses them.

links-missing.description:
Links the config declares without a kind — so it does not create
them — that do not exist, and that no veth or netkit pair in this
apply creates as its peer. A typo, or a device not there yet. The
apply fails on the first, before it changes anything, with
[`ErrorDetail::NotFound`](crate::ErrorDetail::NotFound). They
were skipped without a word (#475). So is a parent (VLAN, macvlan,
VXLAN underlay) or master a declared link names that the config
does not declare and that does not exist (#518).

links-to-recreate.description:
Links to delete and create again, because a declared kind
parameter — a VLAN id, a VXLAN VNI, a bond mode, the kind itself —
cannot be changed on a live link. Each one is also in
[`links_to_add`](Self::links_to_add). A refused one
([`LinkRecreate::is_refused`]) makes the apply fail instead (#417).

links-to-remove.description:
Links the previous config declared and this one does not, still in
the kernel with the kind they were declared with, and the links the
kernel deletes along with them. The apply deletes them first, before
any recreate or create. Only with [`PlanOptions::previous`] (#512).

links-to-rename.description:
Peers of declared veth and netkit pairs to rename to the name their
pair declares (#804), before anything else: the rest of the diff
is against the renamed links.

neighbours-to-remove.description:
Neighbours the previous config declared and this one does not,
still in the kernel (#516). Only with [`PlanOptions::previous`]: a
purge leaves neighbours alone.

neighbours-to-set.description:
Neighbours to install with `NLM_F_REPLACE` (#516): missing, not
permanent, or with another link-layer address — or on a device the
apply recreates, flushes (down, an L3 master move) or gives another
MAC, which loses them.

nexthops-refused.description:
Declared nexthops the apply refuses to install (#516): the id is
another tool's, or the change is between a group and a single
nexthop, which the kernel will not replace. The apply fails on the
first, before it changes anything.

nexthops-to-remove.description:
Nexthop objects the previous config declared and this one does
not, still in the kernel with the config's protocol, groups before
their members (#516). Only with [`PlanOptions::previous`].

nexthops-to-set.description:
Nexthop objects to install with `NLM_F_REPLACE` (#516), single
nexthops before the groups made of them: missing, or different —
or on a link the apply deletes or flushes, which the kernel deletes
them with.

qdiscs-to-remove.description:
Qdiscs the previous config declared and this one does not, still in
the kernel: the apply deletes them, and the kernel puts its default
back. Only with [`PlanOptions::previous`] (#512).

qdiscs-to-replace.description: Qdiscs to replace (same position, different config).

routes-refused.description:
Declared routes the apply refuses to install, because the only
place they could go holds a route nlink does not own (#469). The
apply fails on the first, before it changes anything.

routes-to-remove.description:
Routes to remove.

Always: a route a declared route *supersedes* — same destination,
table, type, gateway and device, a different metric. A replace
only replaces a route of the same metric, so without this a metric
change left the old route installed, and winning (#468).

Under [`PlanOptions::purge`], also every route nothing declared
carries, compared on the full identity (gateway, device, metric,
type), not on `(dst, prefix, table)`. Restricted to the tables the
config owns, to IPv4/IPv6, and to admin/user-managed protocols
(`static` / `boot`); kernel, RA, DHCP and redirect routes are
excluded so dynamic and auto-configured routing is never
clobbered.

rules-to-add.description: Rules to add (#516): none with the config's protocol matches them.

rules-to-remove.description:
Rules the previous config declared and this one does not, still in
the kernel with the config's protocol (#516). Only with
[`PlanOptions::previous`].

tc.description:
The declared TC trees that differ from the kernel's, one per device
(#514).

veth-peers-to-modify.description:
Veth peers to change in the namespace they live in (#680): their
declared MAC, MTU and state.

vrf-strict-mode.description:
The namespace's VRF strict mode to set, where the config declares
another than it has (#680).

CtHelperObject.description:
A conntrack helper object (#703): `ct helper <name> { type "<helper>"
protocol <proto>; [l3proto ip|ip6;] }`, which a rule assigns with
[`Rule::set_ct_helper`](super::Rule::set_ct_helper). The helper module
(`nf_conntrack_ftp`, …) must be loadable.

family.description:
Its layer-3 family, `NFPROTO_IPV4` or `NFPROTO_IPV6`; `None`, the
table's (both, in an inet table).

CtMarkAction.description: What a rule does to the connection mark.

oneOf.description: `ct mark save`: the packet's mark into the connection.
`ct mark restore`: the connection's mark onto the packet.

DeclaredChain.description:
A declared chain — name + optional base-chain hook spec.
Non-base (regular) chains omit the hook fields.

DeclaredFdb.description:
A declared FDB entry (#516): a static or local entry in a bridge, or a
VXLAN remote. See [`NetworkConfig::fdb`].

dev.description: The bridge port, or the VXLAN device.

dst.description: A VXLAN remote: the entry goes in the device's own table.

local.description:
The bridge's own MAC (`permanent`), rather than one forwarded to the
port (`static`).

vlan.description:
The bridge VLAN; none is the untagged entry, and on a VLAN-filtering
bridge one per VLAN of the port as well.

DeclaredFlowtable.description: A declared flowtable inside a table.

addr-gen-mode.description: How the kernel makes the IPv6 link-local address.

address.description:
Hardware address, round-tripped as the canonical
`aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff` string rather than a raw byte array.

altnames.description: The alternative names: exactly these, when declared.

bridge.description: A bridge's own options (#516): VLAN filtering, STP, timers.

gro-max-size.description: The largest GRO packet, in bytes.

gso-max-segs.description: The most segments of a GSO packet.

gso-max-size.description: The largest GSO packet, in bytes.

ipv4-conf.description:
IPv4 per-device settings by sysctl name (`rp_filter`, `forwarding`,
…), set over netlink before the link comes up.

ipv6-conf.description:
IPv6 per-device settings by sysctl name (`accept_dad`,
`disable_ipv6`, …), written to `/proc/sys` in the link's namespace
before it comes up.

ipv6-token.description: The IPv6 interface identifier token (`ip token`).

port.description: A bridge port's options (#516): learning, flooding, isolation, …

protodown.description: Held down for a control plane (only devices that implement it).

DeclaredLinkType.description:
Link type for declared configuration.

# Changing a live link's kind or parameters

The diff compares the kind and every parameter here that the kernel
reports back in the link dump. What a live link can take is changed in
place: a VXLAN's remote, local address and underlay, a bond's
`miimon`, delays, `xmit_hash_policy`, `min_links` and `resend_igmp`, a
macvlan's mode (except into or out of passthru), netkit policies. The
rest — the kind itself, a VLAN's id, protocol or parent, a VXLAN's VNI
or port, a bond's mode, `lacp_rate` or `ad_select`, a macvlan's parent,
a VRF's table — the kernel cannot change on a live link, so the apply
deletes the link and creates it again, putting back what the config
declares on it (see [`ConfigDiff::links_to_recreate`]). It refuses
instead if the link carries something the config does not declare —
including what a config cannot declare: FDB entries someone added,
permanent and proxy neighbours, nexthop objects, multipath routes and
routes through a nexthop object, on the link or on the ports a deleted
bond or VRF flushes as it releases them.
A netkit pair's mode and scrubbing are never changed: recreating the
pair would delete a peer that usually lives in another namespace.

An optional parameter left out is compared against the kernel's
default where the kernel fixes one (a VLAN is 802.1Q; a VXLAN has no
remote, local address or underlay; netkit is L3 and forwards), and not
compared where the default is a module parameter (the VXLAN port, every
bond option).

[`ConfigDiff::links_to_recreate`]: super::ConfigDiff::links_to_recreate

peer_address.description:
The peer's MAC, in its namespace (#680). A peer in this
namespace is declared as a link of its own instead.

peer_mtu.description: The peer's MTU, in its namespace (#680).

peer_netns.description:
The namespace the peer lives in (#516). Unset, the apply creates
the peer here and leaves it wherever it is moved — a CNI moving
it into a container is not undone. Set, the peer is kept there:
one elsewhere, here included, is recreated in it.
[`NetnsRef::Default`](crate::netlink::namespace::NetnsRef::Default)
is this namespace.

peer_state.description: The peer's state, in its namespace (#680).

protocol.description:
VLAN tagging protocol; `None` == kernel default
(802.1Q). Use [`VlanProtocol::Dot1ad`] for Q-in-Q.

local.description:
Tunnel source IP (`IFLA_VXLAN_LOCAL` /
`IFLA_VXLAN_LOCAL6`), either family — but the same family as
`remote`; the kernel refuses a VXLAN that mixes them.

port.description:
UDP destination port (`IFLA_VXLAN_PORT`). Left out, the
kernel uses the `vxlan` module's `udp_port` parameter — 8472
unless set, not the IANA 4789.

oneOf.description: Ipvlan interface (#516): it shares its parent's MAC.
Macvtap interface (#516): a macvlan with a tap queue.
IPv6 tunnel, IPv6 or IPv4 over IPv6 (#516).
GRE over IPv6 (#516); its `mode` is unused.
GRE over IPv6 carrying Ethernet (#516); its `mode` is unused.

IPsec virtual tunnel interface over IPv6 (#680); its `mode`, hop
limit and encapsulation limit are unused.

ERSPAN tunnel over IPv4 (#680): a gretap that wraps what it mirrors
in an ERSPAN header.

XFRM (IPsec) interface (#516): routed traffic meets the IPsec
policies with its `if_id`. The if_id changes in place; a new
underlay, which `xfrmi_changelink` refuses, recreates it.

underlay_dev.description: The device its packets leave through.

oneOf.description:
Geneve tunnel (#516). The VNI, port and the remote's family are
fixed at create; the remote, TTL and TOS change in place.

port.description: The UDP port; the kernel's 6081 when unset.

oneOf.description:
MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE) link on `parent` (#516). The SCI and port are
fixed at create; encryption, protection, SCI inclusion and the
replay window change in place. Its keys and SAs are the MACsec
Generic Netlink API's, not a declaration's.

replay_window.description: Replay protection with this window; unset leaves it alone.

sci.description:
The Secure Channel Identifier, MAC then port as `ip macsec`
shows it; the kernel derives one from the parent's MAC and
[`port`](Self::Macsec::port) when unset.

oneOf.description:
Bare UDP tunnel (#516): an L3 tunnel of `ethertype` over UDP `port`.
It has no changelink, so any change is a recreate. Unverified on a
live kernel: the one these were written on does not build it.
Bond interface. Plan 190 §8 added 5 new option knobs.

downdelay.description:
Time (ms) to wait before disabling a slave on
link-down. Plan 190 §8.

resend_igmp.description:
Number of IGMP membership reports to resend on
failover. Plan 190 §8.

updelay.description:
Time (ms) to wait before enabling a slave on
link-up. Plan 190 §8.

xmit_hash_policy.description:
Typed since 0.31: as a raw `u8`, the create path dropped an
invalid value and the in-place update sent it, so every apply
after the first failed with `EINVAL` (#476).

oneOf.description:
VRF (Virtual Routing & Forwarding) — table-scoped
forwarding domain. Members enslave via
[`LinkBuilder::master`]. Plan 190 §2.3.

OpenVPN data-channel-offload link (kernel 6.16+).
Link-half only — peer / cipher config goes through
the GENL `ovpn` family (Plan 197 / 0.20). Plan 190 §2.3b.

peer_policy.description: Default policy on the peer interface.

peer_scrub.description: Scrub mode on the peer interface (kernel 6.10+).

primary_policy.description: Default policy on the primary peer.

scrub.description: Scrub mode on the primary peer (kernel 6.10+).

oneOf.description: Existing physical interface (not created, only configured).

DeclaredNeighbour.description:
A declared neighbour (#516): a permanent ARP or ND entry with its
link-layer address, or a proxy entry. See
[`NetworkConfig::neighbour`] and [`NetworkConfig::proxy_neighbour`].

lladdr.description:
Its link-layer address, as `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`; none for a proxy
entry.

proxy.description: A proxy entry: the device answers for the address.

blackhole.description: Drop what is routed to it.

group.description: The members of a group, `[id, weight]`, weight 1 and up.

id.description: The id routes name it by; not 0.

ipv6.description: An IPv6 nexthop with no gateway (a blackhole, or a device alone).

onlink.description: The gateway is on the link whatever the subnets say.

DeclaredObject.description:
A declared named stateful object — a counter, quota or limit.

Reconciled by name and type. Only the configuration is compared, never
the live state, so a counter keeps counting and a quota keeps what it has
used across applies. A changed quota is updated in place and keeps its
consumption. A limit cannot be updated (the kernel accepts the message
and changes nothing), so a changed limit is deleted and recreated, and
the rules using it move out of the way and back to their places.

handle.description:
The qdisc's handle, in tc(8) notation in JSON (`"1:"`). `None`: `1:`
for a classful kind, so its classes and filters can name it, and
the kernel's choice for the others (#514).

DeclaredRule.description: A declared policy routing rule (#516). See [`NetworkConfig::rule`].

fwmask.description: The mask the mark is compared under; the kernel's is all ones.

invert.description: Match what the selectors do not (`not`).

ipv6.description: An IPv6 rule; implied by an IPv6 `from` or `to`.

priority.description:
Its place in the rule list (`pref`). Required: the kernel would
pick one, and a rule is known by it.

suppress-prefixlen.description:
Ignore a lookup whose route's prefix is this long or shorter
(`suppress_prefixlength`).

DeclaredRule2.description:
A declared rule — owning table + chain + the typed `Rule`
body. Optional `handle_key` for stable diff identity across
reapplies.

Without a `handle_key`, the diff derives one from the rule's chain,
body and comment (#389), so the rule converges like a keyed one; but
a change to its body gives it a new key, which is a delete and an add
rather than an in-place replace. Give a rule that will change a key
with `DeclaredTableBuilder::rule_keyed`.

DeclaredSet.description:
A declared named set — name, key type, flags, optional size and
timeouts, and its declared elements.

Reconciled by **name** (created if absent in the kernel, deleted
if removed from the config). A changed `key_type` or `flags` cannot
be applied to an existing set, so the set is deleted and recreated
with its declared elements. A changed `size`, `timeout` or
`gc_interval` is applied in place (kernel 6.5+). The declared
`elements` are reconciled per the set's [`SetElementMode`]: by default
exactly for a plain set — missing keys added, undeclared ones removed —
and only added for a set rules write to ([`DeclaredSetBuilder::dynamic`])
or whose elements time out, so that what the packet path put there
stays.

DeclaredTable.description:
A declared table — name, family, flags, and nested chains +
rules + flowtables.

Duration.description: A time, as tc(8) writes it ("10ms", "1.5s", "250us"), or a number of microseconds.

ElementStatement.description:
A statement a set element carries of its own (#703), from a
[`DynsetExpr`] that adds it: the stateful expressions
`nft_set_elem_expr_alloc` accepts.

oneOf.description: `ct count [over] N`: the element's own connection count.

over.description: Match over `count` instead of up to it.

ErspanDirection.description: The direction a type III ERSPAN header says traffic was mirrored in.

ErspanParams.description:
An ERSPAN tunnel's parameters (#680): an `erspan`'s ends are IPv4, an
`ip6erspan`'s IPv6. Each one unset is the kernel's default and is not
compared; a change sends them all, since `erspan_changelink` rebuilds
the configuration from the request.

session.description: The session id, the GRE key both ways: 10 bits, up to 1023.

ttl.description: The outer TTL, or hop limit.

underlay-dev.description: The device the tunnel's packets leave through.

version.description:
The ERSPAN header: type II with its index, or type III with its
direction and hardware id.

ErspanVersion.description: The ERSPAN header an `erspan` or `ip6erspan` tunnel writes (#680).

oneOf.description: Type II (`erspan_ver 1`), with the port `index` it mirrors: 20 bits.

Type III (`erspan_ver 2`), with the direction the traffic was
mirrored in and a 6-bit hardware id.

FilterKeyRepr.description: A filter's own key, for a removal.

actions.description: A flower's or matchall's actions, in order.

estimator.description:
The actions' rate estimator, tc(8)'s `<interval> <time constant>`
(`1s 8s`), which a police `avrate` needs (#792).

params.description: tc(8)'s words for its keys: `ip_proto tcp dst_port 22 classid 1:10`.

parent.description: The qdisc or hook it hangs off (`1:`, `ffff:`).

redirect-to.description: Everything, redirected out of this device (the IFB redirect).

FirewallChain.description: One firewall chain besides input: its policy and rules.

FirewallConfig.description:
Firewall configuration (nftables): one `nlink-lab` table per node.

`policy` and `rules` are the **input** chain (traffic to the node
itself) — the shape every earlier version wrote, so it keeps loading.
`forward` (traffic routed through the node) and `output` (traffic the
node sends) are separate chains with their own policy.

forward.description:
Forward chain. Left out, it is installed with policy accept and no
rules (before 0.14 it took the input chain's policy and could hold
no rule, so `policy drop` on a router dropped everything routed).

output.description: Output chain. Left out, none is installed.

rules.description: Input chain rules, in order (first match wins).

sets.description: Named sets rules match against (`src @blocked`), by name.

burst.description: Packets allowed above the rate in a burst (the kernel's default is 5).

over.description: Act on the packets *above* the rate instead.

group.description: Send to nflog group N instead of the kernel log.

prefix.description: Text put before each logged packet.

clamp_mss.description: `clamp mss N|pmtu`: lower a TCP SYN's MSS option.

classify.description:
`classify X:Y`: the packet's priority, which a `prio` qdisc turns
into a band and an HTB into a class (tc hex: `1:10` is minor 0x10).

counter.description: Count the packets and bytes the rule acts on (`counter`).

counter_name.description:
Count into a named counter (`counter name ssh-drops`), which
`validate { counter … }` and `inspect` read. Declared by use.

ct_mark.description: `ct mark set V`, `ct mark save`, `ct mark restore` (connmark).

limit.description:
Rate limit: the rule acts only on packets under (or, with `over`,
above) the rate.

log.description: Log the packets the rule acts on.

match.description:
Match expression (e.g., "tcp dport 80", "ct state established,related").
Empty or absent: the rule matches every packet.

reject_with.description:
How a `reject` answers. Left out: ICMP port unreachable (ICMPv6
for IPv6).

set_mark.description: `mark set V[/M]`: set the packet mark (only the bits under the mask).

FirewallSet.description:
A named nftables set (`set blocked [10.0.0.0/8, 192.0.2.7]`): what a
rule's `@name` looks up. An nftables set holds one key type, so an IPv4
and an IPv6 blocklist are two sets.

dynamic.description:
Filled at run time (by hand, `nft add element`): `apply` adds the
declared elements and leaves the others.

elements.description:
Elements as written: an address, a prefix (`10.0.0.0/24`), a range
(`10.0.0.1-10.0.0.9`, `8000-8999`), or for a concatenated key its
parts joined by ` . ` (`10.0.1.10 . 22`). A prefix or a range makes
it an interval set.

key.description: The key: one field, or several concatenated (`ipv4 . port`).

FlowtableUpdate.description:
A flowtable changed in place: devices added and removed, flags set
(#479). A new priority or hardware-offload setting cannot be changed on
a live flowtable, so that is a delete and add instead
([`NftablesDiff::flowtables_to_delete`] and
[`NftablesDiff::flowtables_to_add`] both name it).

default_class.description:
The minor of the class unclassified traffic goes to; without one,
it is dropped.

Hook.description:
Netfilter hook point.

**Plan 211 M1 (0.19) breaking change**: `Ingress` was split into
`NetdevIngress` and `InetIngress` because the kernel hook
numbers differ by family. Pre-0.19 the singular `Ingress`
always encoded `0`, which was correct only for
`Family::Netdev` / `Family::Bridge` (`NF_NETDEV_INGRESS = 0`).
On `Family::Inet`/`Ipv4`/`Ipv6`, ingress is
`NF_INET_INGRESS = 5`, so the old encoding installed the
chain on `Prerouting` instead — silent wrong-hook attachment.

`NetdevEgress` is also new (`NF_NETDEV_EGRESS = 1`).

Migration: callers must pick the variant matching the chain's
family. Use [`Hook::is_valid_for_family`] to validate at
build time.

oneOf.description:
Ingress hook for `Family::Inet` / `Family::Ipv4` /
`Family::Ipv6`. Encodes `NF_INET_INGRESS = 5`. Available
since kernel 5.10.

Egress hook for `Family::Netdev`. Encodes
`NF_NETDEV_EGRESS = 1`. Available since kernel 5.16.

default_class.description: The minor of the class unclassified traffic goes to.

loss.description:
Packet loss, in `tc`'s grammar: independent loss (`"0.1%"`), or a
netem Markov model for **bursty** loss — Gilbert-Elliott
`"gemodel p [r [1-h [1-k]]]"` (e.g. `"gemodel 1% 30% 50% 0.1%"`) or
the 4-state `"state p13 [p31 [p32 [p23 [p14]]]]"` (#153). A model's
values and defaults are nlink's, checked against iproute2.

loss_correlation.description:
netem's loss "correlation" (e.g., "25%"). **It does not make loss
bursty, it lowers the loss rate**: netem averages each random draw
with the previous one, so a small loss probability almost never
triggers (`loss 0.5%` with `loss-correlation 25%` drops ~0 %). See
[`Impairment::loss_correlation_warning`].

ImpairmentChange.description: A change to an impairment on a specific endpoint.

oneOf.description: Either IPv6 or IPv4 (`any`): the kernel's default, and `ip link`'s.

Ip6tnlParams.description:
An ip6tnl tunnel's parameters (#516). Each one unset is the kernel's
default (no address, hop limit inherited, an encapsulation limit of 0,
no underlay device) and is not compared; a change sends them all, since
`ip6_tnl_changelink` takes the whole configuration from the request.

key.description: The GRE key, both ways: an ip6gre's or ip6gretap's only.

mode.description: What it carries; either by default. An ip6tnl's only.

underlay-dev.description: The device the tunnel's packets leave through.

oneOf.description: Their traffic goes out through the parent.
L2: the slaves see the parent's broadcasts.
L3: routed, no broadcast or multicast.
L3 with netfilter on the slave (`l3s`).

KeptInUse.description:
An undeclared chain, set, flowtable or object in a managed table that
[`NftablesDiff`] leaves in place, because a rule that stays — one nlink
does not manage — still uses it.

The kernel refuses to delete what a rule uses (`EBUSY`), and one refused
message fails the whole batch, so deleting it would fail every apply until
someone removed the rule by hand (#459).

oneOf.description: A chain a kept rule jumps or goes to.
A named set or map a kept rule looks up or updates.
A flowtable a kept rule offloads to (`flow add @ft`).
A named object a kept rule references.

LeafKeyRepr.description: A leaf's own key, for a removal.

LimitExpr.description:
`limit`: a packet- or byte-rate limit, matching while under the rate
(or, with [`over`](Self::over), once over it).

burst.description:
Burst, in packets or bytes as the rate is. The kernel stores a
packet limit's 0 as its default, 5, and nlink sends 5 for it so the
declared rule matches the dump; a byte limit's 0 stays 0.

kind.description: Whether the rate counts packets or bytes (#528).

over.description:
Match once the rate is exceeded (`limit rate over`,
`NFT_LIMIT_F_INV`).

Link.description: Point-to-point link between two nodes (creates a veth pair).

addresses.description: IP addresses in CIDR notation for each endpoint.

LinkChanges.description: Changes to make to an existing link.

set-address.description:
New MAC address.

A declared `address` was stored by the builder and compared by
nothing, so `.link("eth0", |l| l.address(mac))` on an existing
interface produced an empty diff forever and `apply()` reported
zero changes (#275).

set-kind-params.description:
Kind parameters changed in place — a VXLAN remote, local or
underlay, bond timers and hashing, a macvlan mode, netkit policies
— one `name old -> new` line each. A parameter the kernel cannot
change on a live link is not here: it makes the diff recreate the
link ([`ConfigDiff::links_to_recreate`]) (#417).

set-port-options.description: Bridge port options to change, one `name value` each (#516).

set-port-vlans.description:
Port VLANs to add (`+vlan 10 pvid untagged`) or remove (`-vlan 1`)
(#516).

LinkRecreate.description:
A link the apply deletes and creates again, because a declared
parameter cannot be changed on a live link.

The recreated link itself is also in
[`ConfigDiff::links_to_add`](super::ConfigDiff::links_to_add), and what
the config declares on it — addresses, routes, qdiscs, ports, links
stacked on it — in the other `*_to_add` / `links_to_modify` lists, since
deleting the link deletes them.

blocked-by.description:
What deleting the link would destroy that the config does not
declare, and so cannot restore, or why it cannot be recreated at
all. Non-empty means the apply refuses, with
[`ErrorDetail::NotSupported`](crate::ErrorDetail::NotSupported), rather than
recreate the link; nothing else in the diff depends on it then.
Typed since 0.32 (#513); each blocker's `Display` is the text the
list held before.

destroys.description:
What the recreate destroys that the caller owns
([`Owned`]) or the [`RecreatePolicy`] lets go: for the caller to put
back (#513).

preserved-tc.description:
The link's TC tree that the config does not declare, kept to be put
back after the recreate, with
[`PlanOptions::preserve_undeclared_tc`](super::PlanOptions::preserve_undeclared_tc)
(#645).

reason.description:
Why: the parameters that differ (`vxlan vni 100 -> 200`), or the
link it is stacked on.

resets.description:
What the recreated link loses that the config does not declare and
the kernel does not keep: its alias, and a MAC address the kernel
picks again (#513). Its sysctls (`net.ipv4.conf.<link>.*`,
`net.ipv6.conf.<link>.*`) return to their defaults too.

restore.description:
What the recreate deletes, read back as declarations: what its
inverse puts back (#745). On the recreated link the others were
stacked on; `None` on those, and when something cannot be put back.

unrestorable.description:
What the recreate deletes that no declaration can put back, which
leaves it without an inverse (#745).

LinkRemoval.description:
A link the previous config declared and this one does not, which the
apply deletes (#512), with the links the kernel deletes along with it.

Only a link the previous config gave a kind, still in the kernel with
that kind: never a physical or kindless device, and never a link of the
same name another actor made since. Deleting it would also destroy what
it carries; what no config declared there refuses the removal, as it
refuses a recreate.

blocked-by.description:
What deleting it would destroy that no config declares. Non-empty
means the apply refuses, with
[`ErrorDetail::NotSupported`](crate::ErrorDetail::NotSupported).

destroys.description:
What deleting it destroys that the caller owns or the
[`RecreatePolicy`] lets go (#513).

stacked-on.description:
The removed link it is stacked on, for one the kernel deletes with
it.

unrestorable.description:
What deleting it takes that no declaration can put back, which
leaves the removal without an inverse (#745).

LinkRename.description:
A veth's or netkit's peer the apply renames to the name its pair
declares (#804). The peer is down for the rename, which the kernel
refuses on a running device, and comes back up after it.

peer-of.description: The veth or netkit link whose peer it is.

LinkRestore.description:
What deleting a link takes with it, read back as declarations: what an
undo puts back (#745). The inverse of a
[`DeleteForRecreate`](super::Step::DeleteForRecreate) or
[`RemoveLink`](super::Step::RemoveLink) step.

links.description:
The deleted links as they were, lower devices first: the link, and
the links the kernel deleted with it. The second end of a pair is
declared as an existing device: it comes back with the first.

nexthops.description: Nexthop objects, members before the groups they are in.

ports.description:
The ports the deleted links released, with the master, state and
bridge port options they had.

tc.description: The links' TC trees: qdiscs, classes and filters.

LinkState.description:
Link state (up or down).

The default is [`Unchanged`](Self::Unchanged), as for a link declared
through [`LinkBuilder`] without `.up()` or `.down()`. It used to be
`Down`, which is what serde filled in for a JSON/YAML link that omits
`state` — so declaring only a NIC's MTU in a document took the NIC
down.

MarkValue.description: A mark value, with the bits it applies to.

mask.description: Only these bits; left out, all 32.

MoveReason.description: Why the diff deletes a rule and puts it back.

oneOf.description:
It references a set this diff deletes and recreates; the kernel
refuses to delete a set a rule is bound to (`EBUSY`).

It uses a named object this diff deletes and recreates (a limit
whose rate changed); same `EBUSY`.

It offloads to a flowtable this diff deletes and recreates (its
priority or hardware offload changed); same `EBUSY` (#479).
It is installed out of declared order.

Its chain is deleted and created again, because what changed — the
hook, priority, type or device, or whether it is a base chain at
all — cannot be changed on a live chain (#478).
To what the path allows (`tcp option maxseg size set rt mtu`).

NatProto.description: The L4 protocol a NAT rule matches.

iif.description: Only packets that came in on this interface (`dnat`).

oif.description: Only packets going out of this interface (`masquerade`, `snat`).

proto.description: Only this L4 protocol (`dnat … tcp dport 80`).

NetemLossModel.description:
A netem Markov loss model — `tc`'s `loss state …` and `loss gemodel …`. These are netem's two **bursty** loss generators. `loss

% %` is not one: its correlation lowers the loss rate instead of grouping losses (#369). Read back from the kernel in [`NetemOptions::loss_model`], and set through [`NetemConfig::loss_model`](crate::netlink::tc::NetemConfig::loss_model) or the declarative `QdiscBuilder::loss_model`. Every field holds a probability in **percent** (`0.0..=100.0`), exactly as the kernel stores it, so a model read back from the kernel and one built here compare field for field. Build one with [`gilbert_elliot`](Self::gilbert_elliot) or [`gilbert_intuitive`](Self::gilbert_intuitive), which apply `tc(8)`'s defaults and take each parameter by its meaning, rather than writing the variants directly: Gilbert-Elliot's `h` in particular is the probability of *delivering* in the bad state, the complement of what `tc` takes. Field semantics follow `tc-netem(8)` and iproute2's `q_netem.c`, and were checked against what iproute2 6.15 installs in the kernel. # Example ```no_run # async fn example() -> Result<(), Box> { # let conn = nlink::Connection::::new()?; use nlink::Percent; use nlink::netlink::tc::{NetemConfig, NetemLossModel}; // tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss gemodel 1% 30% 50% 0.1% let model = NetemLossModel::gilbert_elliot(Percent::new(1.0)) // enter the bad state .r(Percent::new(30.0)) // leave it .loss_in_bad(Percent::new(50.0)) // tc's `1-h` .loss_in_good(Percent::new(0.1)); // tc's `1-k` conn.add_qdisc("eth0", NetemConfig::new().loss_model(model)).await?; # Ok(()) # } ```

p13.description:
1 → 3: from good reception into a loss burst. `tc`'s first,
mandatory value.

p23.description: 2 → 3: from good reception within a burst back to losing.

p31.description: 3 → 1: from a loss burst back to good reception.

p32.description: 3 → 2: from a loss burst to good reception within the burst.

oneOf.description:
Gilbert-Elliot 2-state model (`loss gemodel p [r [1-h [1-k]]]`): a
good state and a bad (lossy) state, each with its own loss
probability.

h.description:
The probability of **delivering** a packet in the bad state.
The loss probability there is `100 - h`: `tc`'s `1-h` argument,
which iproute2 converts before sending.

k1.description:
The **loss** probability in the good state: `tc`'s `1-k`
argument, which is sent as given.

p.description: Good → bad: the probability of entering the bad state.

r.description: Bad → good: the probability of leaving the bad state.

NetnsRef.description:
Where a network namespace is, as configs and state files say it.

Owned, `Clone + Eq + Hash`, and with the `serde` feature serializable:
`"default"`, `{"named": "red"}`, `{"path": "/proc/42/ns/net"}`,
`{"pid": 42}`. [`open`](Self::open) gives the [`Netns`] it describes.

oneOf.description: The namespace of whoever opens it.
A namespace `ip netns` knows by this name.
The namespace at this nsfs path.

NetworkImpairerChange.description:
A change to the per-peer impairer on `(network, src_node)`.

`desired` carries the rules that should be live after reconcile;
`None` means "remove the impairer entirely on this source's
interface" (which translates to `PerPeerImpairer::clear`).

NetworkImpairment.description:
Per-pair impairment within a shared network.

`src` and `dst` are node names (not endpoints) — the bridge
determines the interface. The configured `impairment` is applied
to traffic leaving `src`'s network interface destined for `dst`.

impairment.description: netem configuration applied to this pair.

rate_cap.description:
Optional per-pair rate cap (HTB ceil). Independent of
`impairment.rate` — `rate_cap` builds an HTB shaper on top of
netem, while `impairment.rate` uses netem's built-in
(token-bucket-like) rate limiting.

NexthopConflict.description: A declared nexthop the apply will not install (#516).

NftablesChange.description:
A change to the per-node nftables ruleset (firewall + NAT).

`desired_*` carries the rules that should be live after
reconcile; `None` means "remove the ruleset entirely on this
node" (translates to `del_table`).

NftablesDiff.description:
The result of comparing a declared [`NftablesConfig`] against
the kernel's current state. Apply via
[`Self::apply`](super::NftablesDiff::apply).

`is_empty()` returns true when declared and current already
agree (idempotent reapply).

chains-to-add.description: Chains to create — (owning table, owning family, chain).

chains-to-modify.description:
Chains whose policy drifted — (owning table, owning family, chain).
Applied as `NFT_MSG_NEWCHAIN`, which the kernel treats as an update
for an existing chain. What an update cannot change is in
[`Self::chains_to_recreate`].

Until 0.25 a chain's diff identity was its **name alone**: none of
`hook` / `priority` / `policy` / `chain_type` / `device` were compared,
even though `DeclaredChain` carries all five and `ChainInfo` parses all
five back. So flipping a declared firewall from `policy(Accept)` to
`policy(Drop)` produced an empty diff and a no-op apply — the operator
believed the box was default-deny while it stayed default-allow (#200).

chains-to-recreate.description:
Chains to delete and create again, with their declared rules, in
[`Self::rules_to_move`] and [`Self::rules_to_add`] (#478). A refused
one ([`ChainRecreate::is_refused`]) makes the apply fail instead.

flowtables-to-delete.description:
Flowtables to delete — (family, table, name). A flowtable also in
[`Self::flowtables_to_add`] is recreated, its rules moved out of the
way first.

flowtables-to-update.description:
Flowtables whose devices or counter flag changed, updated in place
(#479).

generation.description:
The ruleset generation the diff was taken at, if it was taken from
the kernel: [`apply`](Self::apply) commits only if the ruleset is
still there, and is otherwise refused with `ERESTART`
([`Error::is_restart`](crate::Error::is_restart)) (#482).

kept-in-use.description:
Undeclared chains, sets, flowtables and objects the diff does **not** delete,
because a rule that stays still uses them — see [`KeptInUse`]. Not a
change: [`is_empty`](Self::is_empty) and
[`change_count`](Self::change_count) ignore it, and nothing in it is
sent to the kernel.

objects-to-add.description:
Stateful objects to create — (owning table, owning family, object).
A changed limit is here and in `objects_to_delete`.

objects-to-delete.description: Stateful objects to delete — (table, family, name, type).

objects-to-update.description:
Quotas whose size or `over` changed — updated in place, keeping
what they have used.

rules-to-add.description: Rules to add, each with its placement in the chain.

rules-to-delete.description:
Rules to delete — `(table, family, chain, kernel_handle)`.
Chain is carried explicitly because the kernel rejects a
`NFT_MSG_DELRULE` with an empty `NFTA_RULE_CHAIN` even when
`NFTA_RULE_HANDLE` is supplied (returns `ENOENT`); the
earlier (table, family, handle) shape relied on a kernel
behavior that doesn't actually hold. Plan 178 closeout.

rules-to-move.description:
Declared rules to delete and put back in place.

Rules installed out of declared order move to their place. And a set
whose key type or flags changed is deleted and recreated, as is a
limit object whose rate changed; the kernel refuses to delete either
while a rule still references it (`EBUSY`). So every keyed rule
referencing it is deleted ahead of it and re-added after the new
one, immediately before the next rule in the chain that survives, so
chain order — which is policy — is unchanged.

rules-to-replace.description:
Rules to replace in-place. Each entry is
`(table, family, chain, kernel_handle, replacement)` —
emits `NFT_MSG_NEWRULE | NLM_F_REPLACE | NFTA_RULE_HANDLE`
so the kernel atomically swaps the rule body at that
handle (preserves position, no flush).

Populated by [`NftablesConfig::diff`] when a declared
keyed rule matches a kernel rule by `NFTA_RULE_USERDATA`
comment but the expression bytes differ. Plan 157b v2.

set-elements-to-add.description:
Set elements to add: the declared elements not yet in the kernel
set.

set-elements-to-remove.description:
Set elements to remove: the kernel elements not declared (full
element reconcile).

sets-to-add.description: Sets to create — (owning table, owning family, set).

sets-to-update.description:
Sets whose declared size, timeout or GC interval differs from the
kernel's — (owning table, owning family, set). Applied in place
(`NFT_MSG_NEWSET` without `NLM_F_EXCL`, kernel 6.5+), keeping the
set's elements and the rules bound to it, in a batch
[`apply`](Self::apply) commits ahead of everything else: the kernel
checks element adds against the size the set has *before* the
commit, so a grown set could not take its new elements in the same
batch. An update overwrites the timeout and GC interval with what it
carries, so the set here carries the kernel's where the declaration
has none.

tables-refused.description:
Table flag changes the kernel refuses on a live table — `(family,
name, why)`. Only `NFT_TABLE_F_DORMANT` can change; turning persist
or owner on or off needs the table deleted with everything in it,
which the diff will not do. The apply fails on the first, with
[`ErrorDetail::NotSupported`](crate::ErrorDetail::NotSupported) (#479).

tables-to-modify.description:
Tables whose flags drifted — `(family, name, declared_flags)`. Applied
as `NFT_MSG_NEWTABLE`, which the kernel treats as an update.

Separate from [`Self::tables_to_add`] because every table in *that*
collection has its whole contents (chains, rules, sets, flowtables)
installed wholesale — routing an existing table through it would re-add
everything it already has.

`DeclaredTable::flags` (`.persist(true)`, `NFT_TABLE_F_DORMANT`) used to
be applied only on create, so toggling a flag on an existing table
produced an empty diff and a no-op apply (#208).

tables-to-recreate.description:
Tables deleted and created again, with everything declared in them —
`(family, name, why)`: a changed comment, with
[`NftDiffOptions::recreate_on_comment_change`] (#703). Each is also
in [`Self::tables_to_add`].

ObjectConfig.description: What an object is configured to do.

oneOf.description:
A security mark, by its LSM security context (#703): `secmark
<name> { "system_u:object_r:ssh_server_packet_t:s0" }` under
SELinux, a label such as `"unconfined"` under AppArmor. Given with
[`Rule::set_secmark`](super::Rule::set_secmark); the kernel refuses
a context its LSM does not know.

ObjectType.description:
The kind of a stateful object: `NFT_OBJECT_*`. Only the kinds nlink can
build are named; [`ObjectState::Other`] carries the rest as read back.

Packets.description: A number of packets, or a count as tc(8) writes it ("1000p").

Params.description:
The words of a class, filter or action: one line, or a list where a
word has a space in it.

Percent.description: A percentage from 0 to 100: "1.5%", or a number of percent.

Policy.description: Default policy for a base chain.

PortOptions.description:
A bridge port's options: a link's `port` section (#516), for a link
whose master is a bridge. Each one unset is the kernel's and not
compared. Build with [`LinkBuilder::port_options`].

vlans.description:
The port's VLANs: exactly these, when declared (#516). One the port
has and this does not name is removed, the default PVID a port gets
when it joins a VLAN-filtering bridge included.

PortVlan.description:
One VLAN of a bridge port (#516): `bridge vlan add vid V [pvid]
[untagged]`.

pvid.description: Untagged traffic arriving on the port belongs to it.

PreservedTc.description: A device's undeclared TC tree, kept across its recreate (#645).

qdiscs.description: Its qdiscs: the root and hook qdiscs, and leaves in classes.

targets.description:
The devices its mirred actions send to, by the ifindex they had:
each is looked up again by name when the tree is put back. Written
as `[ifindex, name]` pairs.

QdiscChange.description: A change to the `qdisc` block of one endpoint.

QdiscConfig.description:
A root qdisc other than netem on one interface (issue #67).

Values keep the NLL spelling (`"10mbit"`, `"32kb"`, `"5ms"`) like
[`Impairment`]; the planner parses them.

oneOf.description: Token bucket filter: `rate` and `burst` are mandatory.

ecn.description:
ECN marking: `Some(true)` (`ecn`), `Some(false)` (`noecn`), or
the kernel's default, which is on (#173).

QdiscSpec.description: The document form of a [`QdiscSpec`]: one key per kind.

QuotaExpr.description:
`quota`: a byte budget. `quota until N bytes` matches until `N` bytes
have passed it; with [`over`](Self::over), `quota over N bytes` matches
only after. As a rule expression the quota is the rule's own; as an
[`Object`] it is shared by name.

over.description: Match once the quota is used up (`NFT_QUOTA_F_INV`), not until.

Rate.description: A rate with its unit, as tc(8) writes it: "100mbit", "1gbit", "64kbit".

RateLimitChange.description:
A change to the rate-limit on a single endpoint.

`desired = None` means "remove the rate-limit entirely on this
endpoint" — translates to deleting the root qdisc on the
interface.

RejectWith.description: The answer a `reject` rule sends (`reject with …`).

oneOf.description: A TCP reset. Only meaningful for TCP: the rule must match `tcp`.
ICMP(v6) port unreachable — what a bare `reject` sends.

RestoredNexthop.description: A nexthop object put back, with who added it.

protocol.description: Who added it, by number, as for a route.

RestoredRoute.description: A route put back, with who added it.

protocol.description: Who added it (`ip route`'s `proto`), by number.

RouteChange.description: A change to a single static route on a single node.

desired.description:
`None` → the route should be removed.
`Some` → add (when `was_present == false`) or replace
(when the old config differs).

RouteConflict.description:
A declared route the apply will not install (#469).

A route is added with `NLM_F_REPLACE`, and the kernel replaces the
first route at the same destination, table and metric — whoever put it
there. When that is the kernel's connected route, an RA or DHCP route
or a routing daemon's, replacing it breaks what depends on it: with the
connected route of `10.0.0.1/24` gone, every gateway on that segment is
unreachable. Give the declared route another metric, or remove the
other route.

held-by.description:
The route in its place, as `ip route` shows it:
`10.0.0.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel metric 0`.

RouteNexthop.description: One next hop of a multipath route (#516); see [`RouteBuilder::nexthop`].

dev.description: The device; the kernel's, from the gateway, when unset.

onlink.description: The gateway is on the link whatever the subnets say.

weight.description: Its share of the flows, 1 to 256 (a `u16` since 0.32, #783).

RouteRepr.description:
Serde shadow for [`DeclaredRoute`] — string `destination`/`gateway`
plus the optional knobs, with `type` omitted when it is the
default `unicast`.

destination.description: CIDR-notation destination, or the bare keyword `"default"`.

encap-mpls.description: The labels an MPLS encapsulation pushes, outermost first.

nexthops.description: The next hops of a multipath route.

nhid.description: The nexthop object it goes through.

onlink.description: The gateway is on the link whatever the subnets say.

src.description: The source address for traffic the route carries.

RuleAdd.description: A declared rule to add, and where it goes.

RuleMove.description:
A rule the diff deletes and re-inserts, keeping (or restoring) its place
in the chain.

from.description: Kernel handle of the rule being deleted.

RulePlacement.description:
Where an added or moved rule goes in its chain. Rule order is policy
(first match wins), so the diff says exactly where each rule lands.

oneOf.description: At the end of the chain.
Immediately before the rule with this handle.
Immediately after the rule with this handle.

owned.description: Tag it as the declarative apply's own (#527).

SetDataType.description: What a map maps its keys to.

oneOf.description:
A verdict: a verdict map (`vmap`), whose lookup decides the packet
or jumps to a chain.
A value of this type: a mark, a class id, an address, …

A named stateful object of this type: an object map, whose elements
name counters, quotas or limits ([`SetElement::object`]).

SetElement.description:
A set element: a key, or a range of keys, with what goes with it.

The fields are private so an element can grow — a range end, map data,
a timeout — without a breaking change; build one with the constructors
and read it back with the accessors. How an element is written depends
on the set it goes into (an interval set stores a range as two wire
elements, for one), which is why the element operations take the
[`Set`] rather than its name.

counter.description: Its counter's packets and bytes, as the kernel reports them (#703).

expiration.description: Time left before the element expires, as the kernel reports it.

key_end.description: Inclusive end of a range element.

quota_used.description: Its quota's bytes used, as the kernel reports them (#703).

SetElementData.description: What a map element maps its key to.

oneOf.description: A value, in the map's data type (`NFTA_DATA_VALUE`).
A verdict, in a verdict map (`NFTA_DATA_VERDICT`).
The name of a stateful object, in an object map.

SetElementMode.description: How a declared set's elements are reconciled with the kernel's.

oneOf.description:
The set holds the declared elements and nothing else: undeclared
elements are removed. The default for a set nothing else writes to.

The declared elements are added if missing; elements the declaration
does not name are left. The default for a dynamic set
(`NFT_SET_EVAL`) and one whose elements time out (`NFT_SET_TIMEOUT`):
their elements come from the packet path, and removing them on every
apply would undo what the rules did.

SetElementsChange.description:
Elements to add to, or remove from, one set — with the [`Set`] they
belong to, since how an element is written depends on the set.

SetFlags.description:
Set flags — `NFTA_SET_FLAGS`, the `NFT_SET_*` bits, in the shape of
[`CtState`] and [`TcpFlags`]. Combine with `|`.

SetKey.description: One field of a set key.

SetKeyType.description:
Key type for nftables sets.

Plan 198 §2.1 added `InetProto` (single u8 protocol — e.g.
`tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`) and `Concat(Vec<_>)` (composite key
used in rules like `ip saddr . tcp dport`).

oneOf.description:
A TC class id, `major:minor` (4 bytes, host order) — what
`meta priority` holds. A value type for priority maps
([`Rule::set_priority_from_map`]).

IP protocol number — a single byte (`tcp` = 6, `udp` = 17,
`icmp` = 1); padded to 4 only as a field of a concatenation.
Plan 198 §2.1.

Concatenated key — packs multiple component keys
end-to-end with 4-byte alignment between. Common in
rules like `ip saddr . tcp dport`. Plan 198 §2.1.
Build elements with [`SetElement::concat`] and match with
[`Rule::match_concat_in_set`].

The vector MUST be non-empty (a single-component concat
is degenerate but accepted — the kernel treats it as a
normal key).

SetPolicy.description:
What the kernel picks a set's backend for (`NFTA_SET_POLICY`, #703):
lookup speed, the default, or memory.

oneOf.description: `policy performance`, the default; the kernel does not dump it.

depth.description: The most packets a flow queues (#806).

divisor.description: Hash buckets, a power of two (#806).

headdrop.description: Drop from the head of a full flow's queue (#806).

perturb.description: Whole seconds; a fraction rounds up.

SysctlChange.description:
Sysctl changes on a single node.

We don't try to *reset* removed sysctls — the kernel default
isn't recoverable in general and overshooting is worse than
leaving the previous value in place. Removed entries are
reported so the operator can act on them, but no kernel call
is made on the remove path.

TableMode.description: Who else may put things in a declared table (#527).

oneOf.description:
The config owns the table: a chain, set, object or flowtable it does
not declare is deleted. Rules another tool wrote are still left
alone, unless the chain is
[`exclusive`](DeclaredChainBuilder::exclusive).

Others put things in the table too: of the chains, sets and objects
the config does not declare, only the ones nlink's apply created —
it tags them in their userdata — are deleted, and no undeclared
flowtable is (a flowtable has no userdata to tag).

mpu.description: The least size a packet is charged as (#806).

overhead.description: Bytes added to each packet's size (#806).

TcHandle.description:
A traffic-control handle: a packed `(major, minor)` `u16` pair plus
the special values `ROOT`, `INGRESS`, `CLSACT`, `UNSPEC`.

Internally `(major as u32) << 16 | minor as u32`, matching the
kernel's encoding. Round-trips with `tc(8)` notation via
[`FromStr`] and [`fmt::Display`].

TcObject.description:
One qdisc, class or filter as the kernel dumped it, to be put back as
it was.

handle.description: Its handle (a filter's: the node it is at).

info.description: A filter's `tcm_info`: its priority and protocol.

options.description:
Its `TCA_OPTIONS`, as dumped, in hex: what a class or filter is
put back with.

parent.description: The qdisc, class or hook it hangs off.

spec.description:
A qdisc, read back as a declaration: what it is put back as. A
qdisc's dump is not always a request — HTB reports its version in
a form its init refuses — so qdiscs go back through the typed path.

TopologyDiff.description: A structured diff between two topologies.

network_impairs_changed.description:
Network-level per-pair impairment changes, grouped by
`(network_name, src_node)` because that's the unit
`nlink::netlink::impair::PerPeerImpairer` reconciles.

nftables_changed.description:
Per-node nftables ruleset changes (firewall + NAT, both
rooted in the same `nlink-lab` table). One entry per node whose
rules differ; the `nftables` layer has the per-rule detail. The
apply reconciles rule by rule in one atomic batch. Plan 152
Phase B.

rate_limits_changed.description: Per-endpoint rate-limit changes. Plan 152 Phase B.

routes_changed.description: Per-node static-route changes. Plan 152 Phase B.

sysctls_changed.description: Per-node sysctl changes. Plan 152 Phase B.

TunnelParams.description:
An IPv4 tunnel's parameters (#516): a gre, gretap, ipip, sit or vti
link. Each one unset is the kernel's default (no address, TTL inherited,
no key, no underlay device), and a change sends them all: a tunnel's
`changelink` takes its whole configuration from the request.

key.description: The key, both ways (gre, gretap and vti only).

ttl.description:
The outer TTL (not for vti). Unset is the kernel's — inherit for
gre and ipip, 64 for sit — and not compared.

underlay-dev.description: The device the tunnel's packets leave through.

Verdict.description:
Rule verdict.

`#[non_exhaustive]` so new variants can be added additively.
[`Verdict::JumpTo`] and [`Verdict::GotoTo`] carry a validated
[`ChainName`] — interior NULs / overlong / empty names are
rejected at construction rather than at kernel apply time.

(The 0.20.1 `Verdict::Jump(String)` / `Verdict::Goto(String)`
variants were removed in 0.21.)

oneOf.description:
Jump to a named chain (push-and-continue). Validated against
the kernel chain-name contract at construction.

Goto a named chain (tail-call). Validated against the kernel
chain-name contract at construction.

VethPeerChange.description:
A veth peer's declared settings, changed in the namespace it lives in
(#680): no declaration in this config can name it there.

changes.description: What changes: its state, MTU and MAC.

link.description: The veth whose peer it is.

VlanProtocol.description:
VLAN tagging protocol (`IFLA_VLAN_PROTOCOL` wire value).

802.1Q (Dot1q) is the kernel default; 802.1ad (Dot1ad) is
stacked VLAN encap (Q-in-Q). Plan 190 §2.2.

XmitHashPolicy.description: Transmit hash policy for XOR/LACP modes.
